name: Litti Chokha
description: Wheat dough balls stuffed with spiced sattu, roasted over coal, served with chokha of roasted brinjal, potato and tomato. A Bihari influence, it is a filling everyday meal in Jharkhand.
how_to_eat: Dip the litti in ghee and eat with chokha and papad.
how_to_order: Ask for 'litti chokha' at roadside stalls.

name: Dhuska
description: A thick deep-fried disc of briefly fermented ground rice, chana dal and urad dal, flavoured with green chilli, ginger and cumin; crisp outside and soft inside. It is considered Jharkhand's most iconic street food and a common breakfast.
how_to_eat: Eat hot with ghugni (black chickpea curry) or aloo curry.
how_to_order: Ask for 'dhuska ghugni' at breakfast stalls and weekly haats.

name: Red Ant Chutney
description: A tribal chutney of mashed red weaver ants and their eggs, with a distinct taste. It is eaten by tribal communities in Jharkhand and neighbouring states.
how_to_eat: Eat a small amount as a relish with rice.
how_to_order: Look for it at tribal village haats; it is rarely on restaurant menus.

name: Chilka Roti
description: A thin, dosa-like pancake of rice flour with chana dal (and sometimes urad dal), cooked on a tawa with little oil. It is made for festivals and special occasions.
how_to_eat: Eat with chana dal chutney, a vegetable curry, or mutton curry.
how_to_order: Mostly home food; ask for 'chilka roti' at Jharkhandi restaurants.

name: Rugra (Putka)
description: A wild monsoon mushroom foraged from around sal tree roots, with an earthy, meaty flavour and dense texture; it cannot be farmed. It is sautéed in mustard oil with onion, garlic, dried red chillies and turmeric.
how_to_eat: Eat the curry with steamed rice.
how_to_order: Look for 'rugra' at local markets during the monsoon and ask for rugra curry at home-style eateries.

name: Muri Ghugni
description: Puffed rice (muri) topped with ghugni, a dark, tangy curry of black chickpeas with onion, tomato, cumin and dry spices. It is a cheap, filling everyday snack.
how_to_eat: Eat standing, from a sal-leaf bowl.
how_to_order: Ask for 'muri ghugni' at weekly haats and roadside stalls.

name: Dal Pitha
description: A rice-flour dumpling stuffed with chana dal seasoned with ginger, garlic and mustard, steamed in banana or sal leaf. Munda and Oraon households make it in winter.
how_to_eat: Eat warm with green chutney or a mustard dip.
how_to_order: Mostly home-made in winter and at festivals.

name: Thekua
description: A crisp fried sweet of wheat flour, fennel and jaggery or sugar cooked in ghee, with a long shelf life. It is offered as prasad at Chhath Puja and eaten as an evening snack.
how_to_order: Ask for 'thekua' at sweet shops around Chhath.

name: Malpua
description: A fried, sweetened pancake synonymous with Holi in Jharkhand; the local version is thicker and less sugary, only lightly dipped in syrup.
how_to_order: Mostly home-made on the eve of Holi; also at sweet shops.

name: Handia
description: A mild, cloudy, slightly sour rice beer made by fermenting boiled rice with ranu tablets, dried cakes of 20-25 wild herbs and roots, for about a week. Munda, Santhal and Ho communities offer it to guests and serve it at festivals, weddings and rites.
how_to_eat: Drink from a leaf cup or clay pot, as offered.
how_to_order: Found at village haats and festivals rather than shops; accept it when offered as hospitality.
